name: SELF_SKEPTICAL_AUDIT
threats: A Python reference model could agree with itself while HIR MIR or native code uses different builder primitives.
A compiler marker could claim zero-copy finish while generated C allocates or copies in a helper.
A view may remain usable after growth if borrow_end is emitted too early or on only one branch.
A no-op reserve could be confused with a growth reserve and hide allocator activity.
Allocator calls and payload-copy bytes could be conflated, invalidating amortized-growth evidence.
Using realloc directly could obscure whether the old pointer remains valid on failure.
The final Bytes and finished builder could retain the same owner and double free it.
Compile-time rejects must not be counted as sanitizer executions.
Repeated parameter seeds must not be presented as independent semantic families.
Benchmark arms could implement different growth policies or checksum work.
Subprocess and scheduler noise could satisfy the timing gate without MAD control.
Post-hoc growth-factor or status-gate changes would invalidate the experiment.
Previous Bytes evidence cannot substitute for BytesBuilder growth, finish, or cleanup evidence.
controls: Freeze policy, status gates, workload, warmup count, measured count, and slowdown threshold before implementation.
Use one parameterized state-machine corpus with independent family labels and deterministic seeds.
Compare reference, surface HIR, unoptimized MIR, optimized MIR, and actual native binary outputs.
Expose builder_create, builder_grow, payload_copy, finish transfer, and drop as auditable MIR operations.
Count allocations, frees, reallocations, growth bytes, extend bytes, and finish copies separately.
Use malloc-copy-free growth so old-buffer release ordering is visible and failure safe.
Run ASan, UBSan, and LeakSanitizer only on executed native builder paths.
Add deliberate finish-copy, missing-free, and live-view-append falsification controls.
Run the six benchmark arms with deterministic randomized sequential order and one-CPU affinity.
Run exactly one Decision corpus and one full test suite after quick-loop stabilization.
Freeze old Bytes artifact hashes and do not rerun their benchmarks.
post_hoc_status: Status names, capacity policy, corpus minima, performance ratio, sanitizer requirement, and full-suite requirement remain fixed until final artifact validation.
